en: Oṃ, salutations to Śiva!
Salutations to the Supreme Lord, the Lord of the Gaṇas, the wielder of the trident,
who is seated upon the lotus-throne of consciousness, whose form is divided fourfold.
Having meditated upon the Supreme Lord as all-pervasive, devoid of color and sound,
Śiva-hood clearly arises for yogins in this manner even during the state of emergence.
Then the yogi, consisting of power (śakti) and having a body whose essence is sound (nāda) and the point (bindu),
attains the perfection of the dyad while abiding in the supportless state.
Since these two verses have been proclaimed from the mouth of Śiva,
this pure commentary on the *Yogakośa* is here set forth.
The ground consisting of egoism is indeed beyond the ground of intellect;
by it all this is pervaded, and it alone is the knower that bestows liberation.
The supreme power of the Lord is non-different from Him, consisting of consciousness;
that very power of knowledge manifests again in the form of mantra.
The *ahaṃkāra* is known as the mantra whose nature consists of Śiva, Śakti, and the Self; that which is its first [syllable], consisting of the letterless (*avarṇa*), is the Supreme Lord Śiva.
That which consists of Nāda and Bindu is the second power, the divine;
these two are declared to be the seed-nature of all that is moving and unmoving.
"All phonemes are sealed by this [syllable] which has the form of charcoal;
therefore, yogins who contemplate reality call it the Śabdabrahman."
Having meditated upon that which is breathless and soundless through the vision that is free from division,
one becomes dissolved in the supreme state by means of the yoga of the awareness of pure consciousness alone.
For it has been thus instructed by the Siddhas in a certain compendium of established tenets:
"From the navel upwards is one span (vitasti), and from below the throat is six finger-breadths."
The heart is in the middle region, and within the center of the heart is a lotus;
situated there in its center is a subtle pericarp through which the three paths pass.
In that center, indeed, the letter *A* is established as the reality of one's own self;
within the letter *A* is the supreme, subtle [reality], characterized by the principle of pure consciousness alone.
Bhairava has also taught that its worship consists of recitation within consciousness;
for one who recites the letter *A*, which is without the nasal dot (*bindu*) or the visarga, it is great.
O Goddess, the supreme Lord, the flood of gnosis, suddenly arises;
in the location of the ears, the second power, the sovereign Śakti, is without support.
The seed-state Kuṇḍalinī, whose nature consists of Nāda and Bindu, is this power of breath within the body; known as the syllable *Ha*, she resounds intensely.
Having blocked the openings of the ears with his hands,
the yogi should clearly perceive the Bindu in the middle of the eyebrows— the eternal mother of the universe.
He is constantly perceived by yogins as blazing with his own splendor;
the moon and sun are the two reflections in his left and right eyes.
Having rendered those two supportless, one should rest in the eternal Brahman;
this is also stated in the Vijñānabhairava, the scripture practiced by the Siddhas.
Listen correctly, O Goddess, as I declare this tradition:
liberation arises immediately when the eyes are merely fixed in stillness.
Having contracted the ears and likewise the lower opening,
meditating upon the syllable *an-ak-am-a-hal-am*, he would enter the aperture of Brahman in an instant.
Thus, what was sung from the mouth of the Siddhas has been proclaimed by [the author] himself;
through this path, those who have attained perfection reach the state of the Yoginīs.
This is the work of the son of that Harṣadatta, who was born in Jākaḍeśa and is a lion among the mane-tufts of the Mīmāṃsā.
